summary: Tested the 4 new ops features (fleet trends, archive schedule, alert quiet hours/escalation/ack/digest, upgrade nudges, Slack OAuth start) end-to-end, plus regression. Backend: new tests/test_ops_api.py has 19 tests and all pass. The full suite passes 52/52 after two old tamper assertions were updated (see updated_files). The built-in runner gives 72/72. UI: every listed testid and flow works: trends chart (9 lines), range/metric tabs, drift focus (other lines dim to 0.15), remove AlertDialog cancel/confirm, schedule save/run/pause, quiet-hours save/enable/digest queued -> flush, critical Ack -> acked pill, Slack connect redirects to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with the right client_id/scope/redirect_uri, nudges send/resend with count incrementing. I fixed one real bug: the toast for /alerts?slack=connected never showed. Found 1 real backend bug: the archive schedule can run twice in one day.

critical.issue: Schedule can run twice per day. Moving timeUtc to a later time today clears lastRunDate. Moving it back to an earlier time (already passed) then makes the loop run 'scheduled' again right away. Seen: two 'scheduled' runs on 2026-10-21 (12:23:28 and 12:24:28), both at 02:00. The panel also shows 'next <now> UTC' in that state.

minor.issue: alert_state.escalations is not reset when a new firing episode starts. The UI showed '×3 esc' on an alert that had just re-fired. Reset escalations:0 (and acknowledgedAt) in the $set on each firing transition.

fras_val_008 is breach=true in all ranges but drifting=true only in 7d. In 24h the change (uptime -0.03, vote -0.55, missed +0.38) is below the DRIFT thresholds because the drift profile is spread over 7 days. This may be by design; flagging because the request expected breach/drifting.

Lagging set for epoch 1000 is 003, 004, 005, 006, not 008. 008 runs 6.4.0/4.2.0, which meets the minimum, and lagging uses compliance with frozen=False. This is consistent with fleetReady 5/9, so it is correct, but it differs from the review note.
origin accepts any https:// value and the callback redirects to it. Slack's registered redirect_uri limits the risk, but validate origin against an allowlist or the host header.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent. On a hard load of /alerts?slack=connected (or slack=error) no toast showed. The Alerts effect runs before the <Toaster/> sibling (App.js L41) subscribes. After deferring with setTimeout it showed twice because StrictMode runs the effect twice, so a stable id 'slack-oauth' was added. Verified: exactly one toast and the query is cleared.
Non-numeric input such as 'abc' saves as 0 (Number(x)||0), which silently turns escalation off. Use type=number with validation.
Entering -5 shows the raw pydantic VALIDATION_ERROR JSON in the toast. Use type=number min=0 or a friendly message. The input does reset correctly.

testid nudge-row-<validatorId> is duplicated across epochs (fras_val_005 has rows for 900 and 1000). Use nudge-row-<epoch>-<id>. Send/Re-send give no toast, so a deduped click ('0 sent') looks like nothing happened.

issues: The fleet-drift-count pill says 'N drifting' but counts drifting OR breach. With 24h it shows '1 drifting' while 008 is labelled 'breach'. Consider 'N flagged'.

action_items: Fix the archive schedule double run: store lastRunAt and run only if lastRunAt < today's due time (or never clear lastRunDate on PUT). Make nextRunAt never show a past or now time.
Reset alert_state.escalations (and acknowledgedAt) at each new firing transition in dispatch().
Validate escalation-minutes and older-than inputs on the client (type=number) and show friendly 422 messages.
Make nudge-row testids unique per epoch and add a toast with the sent count for nudge/resend.
Optional: rename the drift-count pill to 'flagged'. Restrict OAuth origin to an allowlist.
critical_code_review_comments: ops.archive_schedule_put: clearing lastRunDate whenever the new time is in the future loses today's run record. This is the root cause of the double run.
ops.backfill only runs if fleet_samples is empty. Validators added later have no history and deleted ones still have samples (harmless, since the series is filtered by the validators list in the UI).
extras.dispatch: in digest mode a warning held during quiet hours gets lastPagedAt set. This is harmless (escalation is critical-only) but noisy.
verify_audit_chain now returns FIELD_MISMATCH before HASH_MISMATCH when payload fields differ from the envelope. Old pytest assertions were updated to accept it.

success_rate.backend: 100% (52/52 pytest, 72/72 built-in), 1 logic bug found by inspection + data
success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all flows work; toast bug fixed; minor UX issues)

seed_data_creation: No permanent seed data. Tests insert lock_samples with TEST:true (result=error) to fire the critical LockAvailabilityLow and delete them afterwards. fras_val_009 was deleted via the UI and re-registered with its seed values. Several archives/archive runs and nudge counts were added (audit-only, expected).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/ -n0 -p no:cacheprovider. test_ops_api uses pymongo from backend/.env to insert TEST error lock samples and backdate alert_state.lastPagedAt for the escalation test. Its fixture turns autoDispatch off during quiet tests and restores it. Final state: quietEnabled=false, quiet 00:00-23:59 digest, escalation 5, autoDispatch on, no firing alerts, digestPending 0, archive schedule enabled 02:00 older=0, fleet 9 validators at seed, readiness GO. Container clock is 2026-10-21. Epoch 900 is in grace (auto nudges sent for 005/006). Epoch 1000 is in announcement.
rca of the issue: Archive double run: PUT archive-schedule sets lastRunDate=None when the new timeUtc is later than now. A later PUT with an earlier time (02:00 < now) leaves lastRunDate None, so maybe_run_schedule sees t >= due and lastRunDate != today, claims it and runs a second 'scheduled' export the same day. Repro: PUT {timeUtc:'23:58'}, then PUT {timeUtc:'02:00'}, wait 60s, then GET archive-schedule shows a new 'scheduled' history row. Slack toast: Alerts effects run before the Toaster sibling's subscribe effect on first mount, and sonner drops toasts emitted before subscription. Fixed with setTimeout plus a stable toast id.
